column1: # declared-reds.tsv — the umbrella fleet's DECLARED-RED ledger.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# scripts/fleet-summary.sh (T109, unified 005/T031) reports the fleet's state
# as TWO numbers, never merged (FR-009→unified FR-251): the count of
# UNEXPLAINED reds ("defect") and the count of reds that are a DECLARED,
# evidenced, STILL-VALID condition ("declared"). SC-008 (unified SC-132) wants
# "unexplained reds reaches 0, from a baseline of 11" to be computable — which
# requires a durable answer to "is THIS check's current red a defect or a
# declaration", separate from check-registry.tsv's `debt`/`exempt` rows (those
# describe whether a SCRIPT is registered as a check at all, not whether a
# registered check's live run currently exits non-zero).
# A row here does NOT mean "ignore this red forever". It means "as of
# next_review, a human or agent read the evidence and it still explained the
# red". fleet-summary.sh treats an EXPIRED next_review exactly like no
# declaration at all — an expired declaration reverts to DEFECT until it is
# re-verified and re-dated, mirroring the same cadence discipline
# scripts/check-registry.tsv's declared-condition rows use (T116).
# FORMAT: TAB-separated, one row per declared-red check.
#   id                 the `check` id exactly as it appears in
#                       scripts/check-registry.tsv (field 2 of a `check` row)
#   lifting_authority   a ROLE (e.g. "operator"), never a named individual
#   evidence            free text: WHY this check's current red is a declared
#                       condition rather than a defect, and what would change
#                       that (mirrors the check-registry.tsv lifting_evidence
#                       convention)
#   next_review         ISO-8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). Past this date the row is
#                       IGNORED by fleet-summary.sh and the check reverts to
#                       being counted as a defect if it is still red.
# A check id NOT listed here that comes back red is a DEFECT by default — the
# absence of a row is never itself evidence of anything, per §11.4.6.
# PROVENANCE. Seeded 2026-09-15 from the umbrella root CLAUDE.md's own
# "Governance and adaptability instruments" section, which is the most
# recently re-measured account of which fleet members are red BY DESIGN. Two
# checks CLAUDE.md documents as currently red are DELIBERATELY left OFF this
# list rather than declared wholesale:
#   constitution-rules-sweep   CLAUDE.md's own words: "Neither class licenses
#                              treating the sweep as green" — of its 96 FAIL +
#                              2 ERROR (of 271), some are known-unclearable
#                              (third-party/staged carriers, defects internal
#                              to the consumed constitution submodule) but no
#                              CURRENT per-gate breakdown was re-measured this
#                              session to say which FAILs those are. Declaring
#                              the whole gate "declared" would hide whatever
#                              fraction of the 96 is a genuine, actionable,
#                              in-tree defect. It is intentionally left to
#                              default to DEFECT until that breakdown exists.
#   push-topology              exits 1 on `monetization` (private repo, push
#                              urls on gitflic.ru/gitverse.ru with no
#                              read-only adapter registered) per CLAUDE.md,
#                              but that reading was not re-measured THIS
#                              session and this ledger does not assert a
#                              stale reading. Left undeclared on purpose.
# Re-derive rather than trusting any row below — the operator can extend this
# ledger at any time, and fleet-summary.sh's own README section documents how.
content-boundary
column3: RED BY DESIGN, not a defect: umbrella CLAUDE.md's "Content boundary" section documents a fully-attributed-by-path (never judged/redacted) surviving-match population across the fleet, following the 2026-09-01 content-boundary incident. The number moves every run because the corpus and the detector both keep improving; it is not expected to reach 0 until the judged-population work (a documented, unstarted operator decision) is done.
